patch.value: Diagnose repeated CLI startup budget overruns and distinguish runner qualification from command regressions

The 2026-09-28 ecosystem review ran the unchanged CLI transport-floor gate against fresh isolated one-item trackers. The first run failed list at 442 ms versus the fixed 419 ms ceiling. A second isolated run failed get 385/362 ms, context 466/433 ms, next 457/440 ms and create 424/398 ms. Source, benchmark code and budgets were unchanged. The SDK import gate initially failed even bare Node at 305/106 ms but passed its isolated rerun. These observations establish repeated local admission failures, not their cause or a production regression. Determine whether runner contention, runtime state or a reproducible command regression explains the changing failures.

Reproduce with recorded runtime and runner-pressure evidence on an isolated supported environment and compare the unchanged base revision; Classify runner qualification separately from product admission without treating failed or unavailable measurements as passes; Fix only the demonstrated cause and preserve every latency and RSS ratchet unless an explicitly reviewed platform correction is supported; Add positive and negative regression controls proving real command regressions still fail and any runner refusal is explicit
A qualified runner passes unchanged supported-runtime startup budgets, and genuine command regressions remain fail-closed with attributable evidence.
Two transport-floor runs failed fixed latency ceilings across changing commands; independent SDK import rerun passed. The broad static invocation therefore cannot be reported all green.
